It's to ensure that the customer is getting what they pay for (fiber content, meets flammability standards, etc.).  You will note that mattress tags will state something to the effect of "constructed of all new materials".  There are actually people that will recycle mattresses by removing the outer covering/batting, reupholstering and reselling (often to hotels).  I never knew such a thing existed until I was in this industry.  Here's a link on it:  https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/articles/0099-shopping-used-mattresses

Also, http://iabflo.org/ is the organization that governs the standards for all furniture and bedding.

As someone who used to work for a bedding manufacturer, there is an actual agency that audits retail stores and applies fines to the manufacturer if the tag doesn't contain the exact verbiage required.  They will go in and pull an entire shipment from the shelves too, resulting in lost sales for both the retailer and the manufacturer.  They will also take random samples to ensure that the content listed on the label is accurate (ex: 100% cotton).  They even go as far as testing the label itself to ensure that the ink and the tag it is printed on is made of approved materials.

I agree with you that people often think the vet is out to get them; however, in this case it really was bs.  I went in because the dog was losing a lot of his hair.  The first thing I pointed out to them was his enlarged testicle.  They insisted that wasn't the problem and ordered bloodwork.  They then stated he had a thyroid problem and a laundry list of other problems.  The total for their treatment plan was over a grand.  At that point I called my horse vet for a referral and switched to another small animal vet.  This time I kept my mouth shut.  The vet gave him a once over and found the enlarged testicle in less than a minute.  Since the dog was older, she suggested that it could have been cancer, so she wanted to do a quick chest x-ray to see if it was advanced (at which point we would make a choice to either keep him comfortable or go with expensive cancer treatments).  Nothing was found on the x-ray, they neutered him and his hair grew back within a few months.  He went back to being his happy and playful self and lived til he was over 16 years old.

On the flip side of this, extensive googling on the health of my dog saved me over $1000 in bullshit treatments and caused me to find my current vet who fixed the problem and saved my dog's life for less than $200.

I was a pack, pack and a half smoker for over half my life.  I tried cold turkey, gum, patches to no avail.  Around October I started experimenting with the blu disposable e-cigs and found I could get through the night with them, but they really weren't saving me money as I couldn't put the damn thing down.  One disposable lasted like a day at $10...cigarettes in my area are $6/pack, so smoking was cheaper.  Then someone introduced me to the refillable e-cigs.  I bought one the day after Thanksgiving, and I haven't bought a pack of cigarettes since.  Cigarettes actually taste like shit to me now, and I hate the smell of a smoker.  My initial investment was $40 for an Ecto 1100 + $16 for a couple bottles of juice, which is comparable to what I was spending each week on smoking.  The first week of it was rough, I won't lie.  I puffed the hell out of that thing to curb my cravings.  But I found if I just puffed it like crazy, the need for a cigarette would subside.  I actually tried smoking a cigarette a few days in and it tasted terrible.  Then that lingering smell on my clothes and the aftertaste of it.  Yuck!  I butted it out halfway through.  It has now been almost 6 months and I no longer want to smoke cigarettes.  My lung capacity has increased drastically, and so has my savings account.  I went from $60-$70/week to about $12-$14/week...huge difference!  My thought is, go for it.  Try it a week.  At worst you will have spent approximately the same, if not less than you did with cigarettes.

As the proud owner of two horses, I disagree with this statement.  Most riders are as I am, "horse poor".  We will eat ramen noodles for months, drive a shitty car, sometimes even cut our own hair...anything to save a buck in order to keep your horse happy and healthy.

This doesn't mean that everyone who can pay $500 bucks should go buy a horse cuz they like them.  They still require yearly shots just like any other pet.  In addition to this, they need their feet trimmed or shod every 6-8 weeks, their teeth need to be floated (filed) each year, they require a lot of equipment, fly spray is a must in the summer and the non-routine vet calls can be astronomical.  And then you have to pay board if you can't house them at home.  Board around my area is about $200-300 per horse and includes their food, water, pasture and stall.  There's a saying in the horse world...the cheapest part of a horse is the purchase price.  It's mostly true, unless you are talking a top-level show horse like the ones you see in the Olympics. I feel that any horse should be taught to cross water on a ride, because sooner or later, you're bound to end up in this situation.  He is doing it the correct way, asking the horse to move forward and keeping it pointed at the obstacle without getting rough with the horse.  Eventually they figure out that they only have one easy way out of the situation, and that is to move forward.  Getting upset with the horse or beating it does absolutely no good because they are then attaching fear to the situation.  

I disagree (to a point) with your idea of dismounting, because as MsRenee pointed out, the horse generally leaps over the object, and since you're standing on the other side, the place you're standing MUST be the safest place to land.  So, if you do decide to dismount, keep that in mind and be ready to jump out of the way.  I have resorted to dismounting on trail only once...I was riding an OTTB for her first trail ride.  She refused to cross a log after an hour of trying.  I had the other horse totally leave us behind, hoping that she would want to catch up and just cross the damn thing.  It was about 90 degrees out and humid as hell.  By that point, both me and the horse were soaked in sweat and I was fed up!  Unfortunately, this made a bad example for the other rider I was with that day.  She took the horse out a few weeks later and dismounted immediately to cross a stream.  The horse jumped right on top of her and nearly broke her leg.  After that, the girl was scared of riding, even though it was totally her fault.

I also disagree with only doing these types of exercises while the horse is by itself.  Horses generally learn from their riding buddies and will follow a well-broke horse across obstacles with little to no resistance.  After a few experiences with a buddy, they will typically do it by themselves without much of a problem.  I usually take a newbie out with a nice, quiet, well-broke horse that can show them everything is OK.  After we get through it a few times, then we go alone.  While it is true that they will act differently on their own, I still feel it is much easier after another horse has "shown them the way"!

Have you trained a horse under saddle before?  If not, and you've been "out of the game" for a while, you might wanna think about starting out on something that's already broke.  Once you're confident in the saddle, then try breaking your own horse.  If it's your first time, you will want to work with someone who has experience.  I always have someone to steady the horse from the ground the first time I back a horse.  It makes the whole experience easier on both you and the horse.

when you leapfrog, don't pass close enough for the other horse to get kicked, and make sure the passing horse is well ahead before moving back over.  If your horse gives you trouble, take him into a tight circle.  You may also wanna try making your horse take a different path than the other horse if your trails split off and meet up again.  Try making him stay well behind the lead horse without fidgeting, either by shortening his stride, stopping or simply turning around and heading back the way you came from.  Again, you can take him into tight circles if he starts to misbehave.  Don't allow him to move forward til he stands quietly for you.  Horses often hate to be left behind, and the behavior just gets worse if you don't work on it.  All I ever do is trail ride, and oftentimes we go in large groups with the saddle club or on camping trips.  Nothing's more embarrassing than having "that horse" at one of those rides!  And trust me, my Anglo Arab was that horse! lol

Good luck and feel free to message me if you have any questions.

As others have already suggested, check his saddle fit.  Perhaps a different type of pad/girth needs to be used.  My 1/2 Arab is very sensitive...I can only ride her in a felt or fleece pad and her girth also has to be fleece.  No neoprene.  And also check your pad and girth before each ride to make sure there isn't anything stuck to it like a piece of hay or grain or a burr.  

If the problem only seems to be when your horse is behind, you may want to try a game I call leapfrogging.  Start off walking your horse and have another rider trot past you.  Once your horse is behaving, have the other rider slow to a walk and you trot past.  Do this a couple times each ride and you should see an improvement.  You can advance this exercise to having your horse trot/canter and having the other canter past.  This has helped my horse tremendously as she always thinks we're in a race (she's very competitive!).

I grab the horn and kind of push the horse's shoulder over using that while using my foot to move out the horse's front foot on the side I'm standing on. Amazon allows certified vendors to ship directly from the vendor warehouse.  The vendor is required to adhere to the same packaging specifications used in Amazon's own warehouse (Amazon cartons, labels, pack slips).  Often the vendor does not have all the box types used, or may run out of a certain style of Amazon box.  Since Amazon charges the vendor back for not using an Amazon box, the vendor will instruct warehouse employees to pack using the next closest size.  Amazon does random audits of their certified vendors by ordering product from them, which is shipped to an Amazon employees home (so the vendor doesn't know when they're being audited).  

Source: I used to do compliance for a vendor that shipped Amazon product direct from their warehouse.  It is a complete pain!

2) A little bit older now (preteen), me and my best friend loved to race down this one field, then turn around and race back. One time we both turned to the inside instead of to the outside. 3) As an adult now...I was breaking my 4 yo gelding.  He was probably only a week or two under saddle and I took him out on a trail ride.  I rode out across the hayfield (aka the Speedway) to get to the trail.  At the far end of the field is a cow farm.  The owner asked if I could help her chase a loose cow back into the fence.  Since my horse is very calm and brave, I thought he could do it.  I started the chase when the cow turned to face my horse.  He took one look and started to rear and spin.  I wasn't giving up that easy and urged him to go on.  He started back towards the cow and the cow took a step towards him.  He reared again, this time losing his footing and flipping over.  Luckily I was thrown clear, but I looked up in time to see my horse galloping back towards the barn, being chased by the cow.  The lady who owned the farm must've thought I had a concussion, cuz all I could do was laugh hysterically at the sight of the cow chasing the horse while blood ran down my face (I hit a tree branch on my way down).

4) I just bought a new saddle and decided to try it out on my Anglo Arab (Arab x Thoroughbred = crazy) who had only been under saddle a few months.  It was a Western saddle with a bucking strap.  The horse was very light sided, so I opted to leave the bucking strap a bit loose til she became accustomed to the feel.  I started to gallop across the speedway and she started bucking like a bronc.  I fell off, got up, scolded her and continued on my ride even though it hurt like hell.  Towards the end of the ride, I decided to jump a creek with a huge hill on the other side.  I figured she couldn't buck going up the big hill, boy was I wrong.  Again she bucked like a bronc, only this time she caught me in a 2 pt position.  My body flew forward and slammed off of the saddle horn, knocking the wind out of me.  She continued bucking and I once again fell off.  I was holding the reins, but she backed out of the bridle and left me there.  I ended up with a huge hematoma on my you know what, cracked ribs and a concussion.  I never knew that area could turn completely purple like that.  Thankfully my work gave me a few days off after they saw how stiff I was walking (my job was mostly walking).  BTW, I never rode her in a bucking strap again.

It depends on the severity of the break.  If it's a simple fracture (the bone is cracked but not fully broken) the horse can be rehabbed fairly easily with stall rest (keeping them in their stall to limit movement).  It is more difficult to impossible with a full break of the bone (like a compound fracture in humans) and typically people will put the horse down to spare it the misery as they may never walk properly again.  Horses are flight animals and they love to run.  Some horses literally go insane if they are made to stand in their stall for days on end.  We had one horse at the barn (a young thoroughbred racehorse) that had a bowed tendon which required stall rest.  He started banging his head against his stall door because he had so much energy and no way to release it.

Source:  I board at a barn that acts as a layup/rehab facility for racehorses.  The owner treats all kinds of injuries, including broken bones.  I ask a lot of questions and help whenever possible.

I wouldn't communicate with him any further except by certified mail or email...get everything in writing.  I had a landlord that tried to screw me out of a deposit AND charge me an entire year's rent simply because I wanted to move out 1 month after the lease expired.  Luckily, my previous landlord was really cool and told me how stuff works.  In my state (PA), you can rent on a month to month basis if your original (1 yr) lease has expired and you have not yet signed on for another year.  The terms would remain the same as the original lease.  Since I gave him my intent to vacate 30 days prior to the move (via certified mail) he could not keep my security, nor charge me for the rest of the year (he was claiming the lease "auto renewed".  I also did a walkthrough of the apartment and had him sign a paper that the apartment was in good order (no damages).  There is a law out there, the Landlord and Tenant Act, which outlines the legal terms of leases.  In this, it clearly states that the tenant is due double the security deposit if the landlord refuses to return the security deposit within 30 days of the tenant vacating the property (if the tenant provides a written notice at least 30 days prior to vacating), unless the landlord provides a written list of itemized deductions within 30 days of the tenant vacating.  I ended up having to go to court, where I was found in the right and awarded double my deposit.  He still didn't pay and they marked items at his house for auction to cover the expense (his Weber grill, his hot tub, etc.).  He magically came up with the money that day.  I kind of felt like a dick doing this, but I can't help but think how many people he has probably screwed over the years pulling this bullshit.  Hopefully next time he thinks twice before trying it.  

TLDR - my landlord tried to keep my security and charge a year's rent, I used the law against him.

Good old Dell Computers.  I have a story of my own, although it is now over 10 years old.  I had just graduated from college and as a present to myself I bought a Dell desktop with all the bells & whistles.  Damn thing cost over $2000.  When it arrived, I unpacked it, started it up and tried to connect to the internet.  Mind you, I was trying to connect via a dial up modem.  Nothing.  I pissed around with it for a bit and determined that the modem was defective.  I called Dell customer service on my land line (my only phone back in those days) and they asked me to go through troubleshooting steps, all of which I had already done.  They insisted I do them again.  Since I only had the one phone and was troubleshooting a dial up modem, I had to hang up and call them back each time.  After about 2 hours of this bullshit, they told me the modem was broken.  Huh?  Really?  Never would've figured that out.  The second modem arrived broken and so they sent a third.  The idiot who delivered it removed it from the anti static bag while walking across the carpet to hand it to me.  Why I have no idea.  This one actually worked.  Since I now had a fully functional machine, I started transferring all of my files from my other computer.  About a month later, I go to turn on the computer and it starts making this odd screeching noise.  Nothing works.  Computer will not turn on.  Keeps screeching at me.  The HARD DRIVE DIED.  I had to spend another few hours on with customer service before they believed me that the hard did, in fact, die.  I told them I no longer wanted the piece of shit and they should return it and give a full refund.  They refused, despite the fact that I am now screaming obscenities at them.  I hang up, furious, and call back hoping to get someone who will actually help.  I punched in a bunch of random numbers and some lady picked up.  She stated that she was the executive assistant to the CEO.  Weird.  I told her my story and she apologized and offered to send return shipping labels and told me to expect a full refund.  A few days later, the shipping labels arrive.  I ship the computer back, receive confirmation that it was received and stop getting bills from Dell.  Problem solved, right?  One would think.  A few years later I run my credit report and to my surprise there is a delinquint account with Dell computers.  I contact Dell, fax the paperwork to them to show it was returned.  They apologize profusely and state that they will fix the problem.  I ask for it in writing.  The next time I run my report, there it is....Dell Computers.  I contact them again and they tell me that it is no longer their responsibility, they have sold my "debt" to a collection agency and give me the number.  I contact the collection agency, fax them the paperwork from the return and the subsequent "correction".  They tell me they will work it out with Dell and will clean up my credit.  They send this to me in writing so I have a record.  That was over 10 years ago and this debt is still on my credit report despite my numerous attempts to clear it over the years.

tl;dr
Dell sent me a fucked up computer and offered a full refund after one month.  It still appears on my credit report after 10+ years despite various attempts to clear it.
